title: Finite directed boundary-capacity Cauchy envelope for the residual cross block
question: Can the R-422 residual cross norm be replaced by an explicit directed boundary-capacity Cauchy envelope, and does the resulting finite reserve remain positive on the fixed Q3 grid?

new_perspective.principle: For disjoint core and tail supports, factor each transformed cross edge as sqrt(c_ij/pi_i) times sqrt(c_ij/pi_j), then apply Cauchy-Schwarz before taking the two-block reserve.
route: Reuse the R-419 conditional Gibbs law, projected momentum conductance, beta grid, orientations, alpha and tail threshold without retuning.
For every eligible row define rho_C=max_i sum_{j in T} c_ij/pi_i and rho_T=max_j sum_{i in C} c_ij/pi_j.
Prove the finite edgewise bound |x^T B y| <= sqrt(rho_C rho_T)||x||||y|| for B_ij=c_ij/sqrt(pi_i pi_j).
Use lambda_capacity=min(a,kappa)-sqrt(rho_C rho_T) as a conservative reserve and retain its positive and nonpositive rows.
Cross-check the bound against the exact restricted R-422 cross norm, independent probes, hostile input controls and a Lean scalar envelope.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: This isolates the boundary-capacity quantity that an analytic common-core proof must control before the residual and coarse Schur sectors can be combined.

finite_theorem.space: Euclidean coordinates after the sqrt(pi) transform, with disjoint core and tail supports
finite_theorem.cross_block: B_ij=c_ij/sqrt(pi_i*pi_j), i in C, j in T
finite_theorem.directed_capacities: rho_C=max_i sum_{j in T} c_ij/pi_i; rho_T=max_j sum_{i in C} c_ij/pi_j
assumptions: core and tail supports are disjoint and nonempty
a is a nonnegative core restricted-form floor and kappa is a nonnegative tail Hardy floor
the transformed cross block contains only the off-diagonal conductance block
finite_theorem.scope_boundary: The theorem is finite and applies row-by-row after the declared split; it is not an analytic boundary-capacity estimate uniform in cutoff, volume, phase or exhaustion.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks the scalar Cauchy-capacity envelope and reserve algebra; it does not formalize the Q3 matrices, directed maxima, common core or any limit.

assumptions: The R-419 conditional law is positive and normalized and the projected conductance is symmetric and nonnegative.
The R-421 tail Lyapunov floor and R-422 block-mean-zero split are reused exactly on the finite Q3 rows.
The transformed cross block is the conductance block divided by sqrt(pi_i pi_j), with no diagonal contribution between disjoint supports.
Directed boundary rates are finite and computed from the same conductance normalization as R-419.
The Lean lane is a scalar algebraic cross-check, not a formalization of the finite matrix eigensolver.
missing_assumptions: A cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform analytic bound on both directed capacities on one Hamiltonian common core.
A positive capacity reserve after combining the capacity envelope with the core and tail floors at all scales.
A controlled two-dimensional block-mean coarse Schur sector and its interaction with the residual reserve.
Two-sided form-norm control of actual R-399 histories and a common split-limit map.
Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification and a sectorwise coercive estimate.
promotion_criteria: Derive the directed capacities from a domain-controlled unbounded Q3 common core rather than finite matrices alone.
Prove a positive capacity reserve uniform in cutoff, volume, phase and exhaustion, including the coarse Schur sector.
Transfer the estimate through R-399 histories and R-415 semigroup bounds before any GNS or physical promotion.
stop_conditions: A nonpositive capacity reserve remains a failure of this sufficient budget and is not clipped or relabeled as a gapless theorem.
A cross norm exceeding the directed capacity envelope stops the lane and indicates a normalization or support defect.
Finite capacity diagnostics cannot be promoted to global Poincare, a GNS gap, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap closure.
evidence_level: T0 / exact finite edgewise Cauchy envelope plus executed Q3-row capacity diagnostic; no uniform theorem or physical conclusion
non_claims: No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform capacity estimate.
No global Poincare or full coarse Schur theorem.
No common Hamiltonian core or split-limit dynamics.
No OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction or sectorwise spectral gap.
No continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.

formal_integration.event_title: R-423 finite directed boundary-capacity Cauchy envelope
formal_integration.lean: R423 PASS; scalar capacity envelope only

boundary: R-423 closes the finite edgewise capacity inequality and records the resulting Q3 sufficient-budget boundary. It does not close the Q3LOCK common-alpha or broken-sector coercivity parents.
next_unlock: Prove an analytic directed-capacity estimate on a common Q3 core, then combine it with the coarse Schur sector and R-399 history transfer.
no_overclaim: A finite capacity reserve is a conditional sufficient budget. Positive or nonpositive rows do not identify the physical vacuum, a regulator-independent gap, a Yang-Mills result or a mass gap.
